title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: Which statement best separates a workflow from an agent when both use a language model and tools?

options.text: A workflow uses one model call, while an agent always uses several
A workflow has no tools, while an agent is given tools to call
In a workflow, code fixes the steps; in an agent, the model does
In a workflow, a person approves each step; an agent runs alone

items.stem: A makerspace assistant is built like this: for every question, the Python code first searches the manuals, then pastes the best pages into a prompt, then calls the model once to write the answer. Is this a workflow or an agent, and why?

options.text: A workflow, because the code fixes the steps and their order in advance
An agent, because the model writes the final answer in its own words
An agent, because it uses a search tool and a language model together
A workflow, because it makes only one call to the language model

items.stem: In an agent, which one decides what the next step is: the model or the program code around it? Answer with the model or the code.

Booking a machine always takes the same four steps in the same order: check the calendar, confirm the slot with the student, write the booking, send a receipt. Which design is the better choice for this part of your assistant?

options.text: An agent, because the model can then invent a better order for the steps
An agent, because booking involves tools and tools need a model to choose
An agent, because students may ask for something different each time
A fixed workflow, because the steps are known and never change

items.stem: Your sponsor's model budget is small. You compare an agent and a fixed workflow that both answer the same simple question correctly. What usually differs between them?

options.text: The workflow costs more, since fixed steps cannot skip unneeded work
The agent costs more, since it may take extra model calls and steps
They cost the same, since the same tools are available to both
The agent costs less, since the model picks only the cheapest path

items.stem: Students' questions vary a lot. One needs only a manual page. Another needs the calendar, then a manual, then the student's training record. A third needs a manual, and then a different manual after the first one points to it. You cannot list the steps in advance. Which design fits this part of the assistant?

options.text: A fixed workflow that runs all three tools for every question
A fixed workflow with one separate fixed path for each question type
An agent, because the model must choose the steps from what comes back
An agent, because agents are always better than any fixed workflow
